clue.text: Advertises professional charges

parts.note: pro is the usual short form of professional
claims are charges or demands for payment, as on an expenses sheet

explanation.surface: A professional's fee is printed on their publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' looks like the professional's fees, but it stands for claims, as in charges against someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim something is to announce it publicly, much as an advert does.

clue.text: A light-weight has reason to hesitate

explanation.surface: A small boxer has second thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: A scruple was an old apothecaries' weight of twenty grains, so a 'light-weight' in the literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny apothecaries' unit of twenty grains; and a moral qualm that makes someone pause before acting.

clue.text: Regarding money supply one can organise in last minute

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters are put inside the word for the last minute

parts.note: the last minute of a match or contest is its final one, so final stands for it

indicators.note: to organise is to arrange, so the letters of one can are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone scrambles at the eleventh hour to arrange what money can be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organise' makes ANCI, which 'in' places within the word for the closing minute; 'supply' completes the definition, since money supply is a financial matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something to do with funds, the cash in circulation, is described by the adjective for finance.

clue.text: Inferior standing — that's material

parts.note: sub as a prefix means below or lesser, as in substandard
a stance is a way of standing or a position held

explanation.surface: A poor reputation turns out to matter after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' is a noun here: physical matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical stuff or matter of any kind is a substance.

clue.text: The French in a group may appear exclusive

indicators.note: in means the French article sits inside the word for a group

parts.note: a sect is a group bound by shared beliefs
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Being French within a clique can make you look snooty.
explanation.definitionFit: A select club admits only a chosen few, so it is exclusive.

clue.text: Southern women with charming ways making changes

parts.note: witches cast charms, that is spells

explanation.surface: Belles from the South with winning manners are reforming things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charming' suggests attractive, but it means casting charms, or spells.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch is to swap one thing for another, so switches are changes.

clue.text: Being forgetful, giving wrong name? Just so!

indicators.note: giving the letters of name in the wrong order rearranges them

parts.note: sic, Latin for thus, marks a quotation as given just so

explanation.surface: Someone getting a name wrong says sorry, they keep forgetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving wrong' scrambles the four letters to AMNE; the 'Just so!' tag is the Latin marker editors put after a quoted slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesic describes someone suffering memory loss, and being forgetful is that state; both work as adjectives here.

clue.text: Outline to read prior to a journey

indicators.note: prior to means the reading word comes before the journey word

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or read carefully
a tour is a journey

explanation.surface: A traveller studies the guidebook before setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: CON for 'read' or study is an old usage, still common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A contour is the outline or shape of something, as a contour line on a map.

clue.text: About a hundred possibly dash for lounge

parts.note: re means about or concerning
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a dash is one example of a line

explanation.surface: Roughly a hundred people make a dash for the lounge bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lounge' looks like a room but is a verb: to lie back at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline is to lean back and rest, just as lounging is.

clue.text: Fly round the hostelry collecting cash?

indicators.note: round means the word for fly goes around the hostelry

parts.note: to wing is to fly
an inn is a hostelry

explanation.surface: Someone darts around the pub with a collecting tin.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as loose: winning is gaining money as a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning a bet or prize means pocketing the money, so it is a way of gathering cash.

clue.text: Sort of car used in war

indicators.note: sort of suggests a version of the words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some kind of vehicle was deployed in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusade was a medieval holy war, and the word now covers any vigorous campaign.

clue.text: His aim is absolute perfection

parts.note: read literally, the man's aim, how he points a gun, is perfect, not his ambition

explanation.definitionFit: An expert marksman never misses the target, so his aim is flawless.

clue.text: Book to keep for oneself

explanation.surface: Booking something means keeping it for yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a table or seat is to hold it in advance; and to set something aside for your own use.

clue.text: Deal made, the commander dined after everybody

indicators.note: after means the commander and his meal come after the word for everybody

parts.note: all means everybody
OC is the military abbreviation for Officer Commanding
ate means dined

explanation.surface: With the deal done, the commander ate after everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' is a verb here, as in dealing out cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To allocate is to share out portions, just as one deals out cards.

clue.text: Cortes arranged for an armed guard

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of Cortes are put in a new order

explanation.surface: The conquistador Cortes organised an armed bodyguard.
explanation.walkthrough: Hernán Cortés was the Spanish conquistador who overthrew the Aztec empire.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort is a protective guard, often armed, travelling with someone.

clue.text: Youth wanted to skin fish

parts.note: to strip is to peel or skin
ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A young lad was wanted to gut and skin the catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripling is a young man not yet fully grown, a youth.

clue.text: Opinions held about people's housing

indicators.note: held about means the opinions word is held around the people

parts.note: tenets are beliefs or opinions
men stands for people in general

explanation.surface: People have strong views on public housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held about' is the container signal. 'housing' looks like a verb but is the definition: crowded rented blocks of flats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenements are blocks of flats, often crowded rented housing.

clue.text: A sailor, some soldiers and a holy man, all side by side

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps
ST, saint, is a holy man

explanation.surface: A sailor, soldiers and a saint all line up together.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Abreast means level with each other, in a line facing the same way.

clue.text: A novice will take ale with spirits in it

indicators.note: in it means the spirits go inside the ale

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
ginn, a variant of jinn, are spirits of Arab legend

explanation.surface: A novice drinker tops up his beer with a shot of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: GINN looks like the drink gin, but it is the jinn or genies of Arabic legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginner is someone just starting out, a learner or novice.

clue.text: The old may be without parking, though it's essential

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the old word goes round the parking letter

parts.note: stale means old and no longer fresh
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: An elderly person may have to manage without a parking space, essential though it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, so STALE goes round P.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple item is a basic one, main or necessary, as staple foods are.

clue.text: Worry about raising golden blossom

indicators.note: about means the word for worry goes around the raised gold

parts.note: to tease is to worry or pester

indicators.note: raising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Fretting over growing yellow flowers in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' makes RO, as a down answer is read upwards, and 'about' wraps the worry word round it. Gold is a heraldic colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea rose is a type of garden rose, valued for its flowers.

clue.text: Leaf-insect display

parts.note: a leaf of a book is a page
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An insect shaped like a leaf puts on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaf-insect' looks like the stick insect's cousin, but the hyphen hides two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a spectacular show or procession, a display.

clue.text: Sweet — of a calmer disposition

indicators.note: disposition means the arrangement of something, so the letters of a calmer are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A sweet person has a more placid nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' is a noun, a confection, not an adjective of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A caramel is a chewy toffee-like sweet made from cooked sugar.

clue.text: Prove a number altered a detail

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a number

indicators.note: altered means the letters of a detail are changed in order

explanation.surface: A small change to one detail can prove a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' rearranges A DETAIL into ALIDATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To validate a claim is to confirm or prove it is true.

clue.text: A daughter failing to get guidance

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
a vice is a moral failing

explanation.surface: A daughter who is struggling seeks counsel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' is a noun, a fault, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is counsel or a recommendation on what to do.

clue.text: Negotiated with constraint and won

parts.note: a bar is a restriction or constraint
gained means won or obtained

explanation.surface: A deal was hammered out under limits and was a victory.
explanation.definitionFit: To have bargained is to have haggled over terms, which is to have negotiated.

clue.text: A man long incarcerated in appalling little place

indicators.note: in means the prisoner is set inside the word for appalling

parts.note: vile means appalling or dreadful
an old lag is a long-serving prisoner

explanation.surface: A lifer is held in dreadful conditions in a small town.
explanation.walkthrough: LAG is British slang for a convict, as in 'old lag', one jailed many times.
explanation.definitionFit: A village is a small settlement, smaller than a town.

clue.text: Drug company accountant — popular egghead

parts.note: CA, chartered accountant, is an accountant
in means fashionable or popular
the head of the word egg is its first letter

explanation.surface: A firm's accountant, a well-liked intellectual, deals in drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual, but it gives the head, first letter, of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocaine is a stimulant narcotic made from coca leaves.

clue.text: Turn cold and green holding on

indicators.note: holding means the cold and green letters hold the word on between them

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: Someone goes pale and green while carrying on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is the container signal. Vert is the heraldic term for green, a convention worth learning.
explanation.definitionFit: To convert something is to change it, to turn it into something else.

clue.text: Such fruit crushes aren't nice

indicators.note: crushes means the letters of aren't nice are pulped and reformed

explanation.surface: Fruit crushes are not pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Such fruit'; 'crushes' looks like drinks, but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach.
